title: Verb る ことになる
shortExplanation: Indicates that something has been decided or arranged; 'it has been decided that', 'it turns out that'.
longExplanation: The る ことになる grammar point is used to express that something has been decided or arranged. It often indicates a decision made by someone else or due to circumstances. It can be translated as 'it has been decided that' or 'it turns out that' in English. The formation requires a verb in る (dictionary) form.

examples.jp: 今日は会議がなくなることになりました。
examples.romaji: Kyou wa kaigi ga nakunaru koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: It has been decided that there will be no meeting today.

examples.jp: 来週、友達と旅行することになった。
examples.romaji: Raishuu, tomodachi to ryokou suru koto ni natta.
examples.en: It has been arranged that I will travel with my friends next week.

examples.jp: 彼女が今度のプロジェクトのリーダーになることになりました。
examples.romaji: Kanojo ga kondo no purojekuto no riida ni naru koto ni narimashita.
examples.en: It has been decided that she will be the leader of the next project.

examples.jp: 急に仕事が入ったので、休みを取ることになった。
examples.romaji: Kyuu ni shigoto ga haitta node, yasumi wo toru koto ni natta.
examples.en: Due to sudden work, it has been decided that I will take a day off.
